OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: GitHub requires an explicit invitation naming a role; there is no default access for non-collaborators. The only collaborator is the owner. GOVERNANCE.md states access is granted at the lowest level that fits the work and removed when someone stops contributing.
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: Branch protection on main requires 1 approving review and 6 passing status checks, forbids force pushes and deletion, and requires linear history. A repository ruleset independently blocks deletion and non-fast-forward pushes.
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: allow_deletions is false in the branch protection for main, and a repository ruleset carries a deletion rule as a second layer.
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: Every workflow declares a top-level permissions block of contents: read, so no job inherits the default write token.
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Jobs raise permissions only where needed: security-events: write only for the CodeQL upload, contents: write only for the SBOM job, id-token: write only for the publish job that signs provenance.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: No CI/CD pipeline in this project accepts an input parameter. No workflow reads inputs.* — the only declared input, dry_run in publish.yml, was removed because nothing read it — and no workflow uses pull_request_target, so no untrusted metadata reaches a pipeline. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/tree/main/.github/workflows
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target. Workflows triggered by pull_request from a fork receive no repository secrets and a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN.
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: No pipeline accepts collaborator-supplied input. No workflow declares or reads inputs.* — the one declared input, dry_run in publish.yml, was removed because nothing read it — so there is no input to sanitize. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/tree/main/.github/workflows
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Semantic versioning with annotated git tags v1.0.0 through v1.0.3, one GitHub release each.
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Release assets carry the version in their filename: the npm tarball and the .mcpb bundle are both named with the release version, which the registry-metadata test suite asserts matches package.json.
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog, and every GitHub release carries notes describing functional and security changes.
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: pnpm with a committed pnpm-lock.yaml, installed with --frozen-lockfile in CI.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: Releases from 1.0.3 are published by CI with a signed SLSA provenance attestation recorded by npm, plus a GitHub build-provenance attestation over the tarball and an SBOM. Verify with: npm audit signatures @shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: Gitleaks runs on every push with a pinned version, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, and credential-shaped test fixtures are assembled from fragments at runtime so no literal appears in source. SECURITY.md documents the policy.
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Secrets and credentials policy": where secrets live, that they are never echoed or written to disk, that forked pull requests receive none, and that exposure triggers rotation first.
OSPS-DO-01.01_justification: README.md documents installation, configuration and usage; the five discovery meta-tools document the remaining tools at runtime.
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Verifying a release": npm audit signatures and the SLSA provenance attestation.
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: Same section. The provenance attestation names the source commit, the workflow file and the runner that built the artefact.
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: SUPPORT.md states that only the latest release is supported and why.
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: SUPPORT.md, section "End of life": a major line stops receiving fixes when its successor ships, with no overlapping window, announced in the release notes.
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Dependency selection": three runtime dependencies, pinned via committed lockfile, actions pinned to commit SHAs, Dependabot through the same gate.
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, section "The gate", and DEVELOPMENT.md give the full build and test commands.
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the members with access to sensitive resources.
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities.
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution looks like, including the read-only guarantee every tool must keep and the coverage floor.
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, section "Granting escalated permissions": a track record is required, activity is reviewed, access is granted at the lowest useful level and removed when dormant.
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: Contributors must sign off every commit under the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1, held at https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/DCO . The DCO workflow checks every commit in a pull request and fails when a Signed-off-by line is absent or does not match the commit author. CONTRIBUTING.md documents it.
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: package.json lists direct dependencies and pnpm-lock.yaml is committed.
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: The sbom workflow generates an SBOM for each release.
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: Six status checks are required on main: tests, both CodeQL languages, Gitleaks, ESLint security and pnpm audit.
OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: Single-repository project with no subprojects or additional codebases. Everything is built from https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp and published as one npm package, https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: No release comprises multiple source code repositories. The project is a single repository, https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp, published as one npm package. There are no subprojects to hold to a security standard.
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: dist/ is gitignored and no build output is committed; the .mcpb bundle is generated and ignored too.
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: The only binary in the repository is assets/icon.png, which is generated from assets/icon.svg — the reviewable source is committed alongside it.
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: GitHub Actions runs the Jest suite (1,014 tests) on every push and pull request, and it is a required check for main.
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, section "The gate", gives the exact commands CI runs.
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests with every change and documents the 100% floor for src/utils/.
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: Single-maintainer project: there is no second person to provide a non-author approval, and GitHub does not let an author approve their own pull request, so no configuration can satisfy this. GOVERNANCE.md records that the project has one member. What compensates: main requires 1 approving review, 6 status checks, linear history, no force pushes and no deletion, and a repository ruleset independently blocks deletion and non-fast-forward pushes. Every change is gated on tests, CodeQL, Gitleaks, ESLint security and pnpm audit, and any owner bypass is recorded by GitHub. This will be met if the project gains a second maintainer.
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md, sections "Security Model" and "Threat Mitigations", describe the actors, the five-layer request pipeline and what each layer does.
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: README.md documents the MCP interface and configuration; the server publishes instructions in its initialize response, and the discovery meta-tools enumerate the rest.
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Threat Mitigations", assesses path traversal, credential leakage, injection, ReDoS and resource exhaustion with the mitigation for each.
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: SECURITY.md covers the attack surface (stdio and optional HTTP transport) and states residual risk under "Known Limitations".
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Reporting Security Issues": acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment within 14, fix released before public disclosure.
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the private reporting channel.
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled; SECURITY.md links to the advisory form as the first channel.
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: Vulnerabilities will be published as GitHub Security Advisories on the repository, and fixes are described in CHANGELOG.md. None have been reported to date.
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: An OpenVEX 0.2.0 document is published at https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/vex.openvex.json and shipped alongside the SBOM with every release. It is generated from `pnpm audit --json` by scripts/generate-vex.mjs rather than written by hand, so it cannot go stale as the dependency tree moves; the sbom workflow regenerates it on every push and warns when the advisories change. Human-set statuses are preserved across runs. The tree currently reports no advisories, so the document has no statements.
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Remediation thresholds": pnpm audit fails the build on HIGH or CRITICAL; MODERATE and below are fixed within 60 days.
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: Same section: no release goes out with a known HIGH or CRITICAL advisory, enforced by a required check rather than by convention.
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: pnpm audit runs on every push and Dependency Review runs on every pull request, blocking newly introduced vulnerable dependencies.
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Remediation thresholds": any CodeQL alert of severity error and any ESLint error blocks the merge; the panel is kept at zero open alerts.
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: CodeQL with security-extended and security-and-quality runs on every push and is a required check for main, as is the ESLint security job.
build_justification: `pnpm run build` compiles the TypeScript sources. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
build_common_tools_justification: TypeScript and pnpm, both widely used in the Node ecosystem.
build_floss_tools_justification: TypeScript (Apache-2.0), pnpm (MIT) and Node.js — all FLOSS, all runnable on a FLOSS platform.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the gate to run, that tests accompany every change, the read-only guarantee tools must keep, and the DCO sign-off. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
crypto_call_justification: Uses Node's built-in `crypto` module. No cryptographic primitive is reimplemented.
crypto_keylength_justification: AES-256-GCM for the audit log; 256-bit keys. HMAC-SHA-256 for session tokens.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The server stores no passwords. Session authentication uses an HMAC-derived token, not a stored credential.
crypto_pfs_justification: The optional HTTPS transport uses Node's default TLS configuration, whose cipher suites are ECDHE-based and therefore provide perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_published_justification: AES-256-GCM, HMAC-SHA-256 and SHA-256 — all published, publicly reviewed algorithms.
crypto_random_justification: `crypto.randomBytes` and `crypto.randomUUID`; no use of Math.random for security purposes.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No MD5, SHA-1, DES or RC4 in any security path.
crypto_working_justification: Default configuration uses no broken or risky algorithm.
delivery_mitm_justification: Published to npm over HTTPS with a signed SLSA provenance attestation. Verify with `npm audit signatures @shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp`. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published by CI, not from a workstation, and npm records the provenance attestation linking tarball to commit and workflow.
documentation_interface_justification: README documents the MCP interface; the server also publishes `instructions` in its initialize response, and five discovery meta-tools enumerate the rest at runtime. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp#readme
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based testing with fast-check over the input validators and detectors. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/tree/main/src/fuzz
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Test assertions are active in every run; there is no assertion-stripping build.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No outstanding findings from dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: TypeScript on Node.js: a memory-safe runtime, so a memory-safety analyser does not apply.
english_justification: All documentation, code comments and issue templates are in English.
know_common_errors_justification: SECURITY.md documents path traversal, credential leakage, injection, ReDoS and resource exhaustion, with the mitigation for each. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
know_secure_design_justification: SECURITY.md describes the five-layer request pipeline and the read-only guarantee. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
maintained_justification: Four releases in August 2026; issues answered.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Gitleaks runs on every push with a pinned version, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on, and both panels are at zero. Credential-shaped test fixtures are assembled from fragments at runtime so no literal appears in source.
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and the notes on each GitHub release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: Security fixes are described in the CHANGELOG and the release notes.
repo_interim_justification: Intermediate commits are on main between releases, not only release snapshots.
report_responses_justification: Acknowledgement within 7 days and assessment within 14, stated in SECURITY.md.
sites_https_justification: The project site and the repository are GitHub, HTTPS only; npm likewise.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL with security-extended and security-and-quality, plus ESLint with the security plugin, on every push.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-extended query suite covers the common vulnerability classes.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every push to main and every pull request, and required to merge.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the suite on every push and pull request. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/actions
test_most_justification: src/utils/ is held at 100% statements, lines and functions with a 90% branch floor enforced in CI; the network-facing transport is at 99.5% of lines.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests with every change. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Every release since 1.0.1 added tests alongside its changes; see the CHANGELOG.
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique semantic version.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities are outstanding; pnpm audit fails the build on HIGH or CRITICAL.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability is outstanding. The remediation thresholds are documented in SECURITY.md.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Acknowledgement within 7 days, stated in SECURITY.md.
warnings_justification: ESLint and TypeScript strict mode; the build surfaces warnings.
warnings_fixed_justification: Zero ESLint errors; the lint job is a required check.
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode and ESLint runs with the security plugin enabled.
access_continuity_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the member with access to every sensitive resource and states what happens if the project stops being maintained. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project is a stdio MCP server with no end-user interface. The optional HTTP transport serves one diagnostic page of plain semantic HTML with no scripts; there is no interactive UI to which accessibility guidance applies.
achieve_passing_justification: The passing badge has been achieved.
assurance_case_justification: SECURITY.md, section "Assurance case": the claim, the three mechanisms it rests on, the evidence for each, where the argument is weakest, and what would falsify it. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The suite spawns the built server over stdio and drives a real MCP handshake, and exercises the HTTP transport against a real listener on a real port including TLS. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/tree/main/src/tests
build_non_recursive_justification: A single `tsc` invocation builds the whole project; there is no recursive build.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The build emits source maps and declaration files alongside the JavaScript.
build_repeatable_justification: `pnpm run verify:reproducible` builds twice from a clean tree and compares a digest over all 3,412 emitted files; it runs in CI. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/scripts/verify-reproducible.mjs
build_standard_variables_justification: Not a compiled C-style build: there is no make, autoconf or equivalent honouring CC, CFLAGS or DESTDIR. The build is `tsc` driven by tsconfig.json.
bus_factor_justification: Single-maintainer project, so the bus factor is 1. GOVERNANCE.md records this openly, and ROADMAP.md names a second maintainer as the highest-value change available to the project. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
coding_standards_justification: ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint and the security plugin, plus TypeScript strict mode. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/eslint.config.js
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The lint job is a required status check on main; zero errors are tolerated.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Cryptographic choices are centralised rather than scattered: the audit log's AES-256-GCM and the session token's HMAC-SHA-256 each live in one module, so replacing an algorithm is a single change. Key rotation with previous-key fallback is already implemented, which is the mechanism a migration would use.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The HTTPS transport uses Node's TLS with certificate verification on; mutual TLS additionally sets requestCert with rejectUnauthorized. The test suite validates against a supplied CA rather than disabling verification.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Keys are supplied through environment variables, never compiled in, and rotation is supported with previous-key fallback so an existing audit log stays readable across a rotation. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_tls12_justification: The HTTPS transport uses Node's default TLS configuration, which negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and does not offer anything earlier.
crypto_used_network_justification: The default transport is stdio, with no network exposure at all. The optional HTTP transport supports TLS and mutual TLS, and refuses to start on a half-configured TLS setup rather than falling back to plaintext.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Session tokens are verified by HMAC comparison; no credential is sent to a third party for verification.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1, with a CI check that every commit in a pull request carries a Signed-off-by matching its author. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/DCO
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot is enabled, and `pnpm audit` plus Dependency Review run in CI on every push and pull request.
documentation_achievements_justification: README, section "Project standards", lists the badges and supply-chain properties achieved. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp#project-standards
documentation_architecture_justification: https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md and the security model in SECURITY.md.
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is updated in the same commit as the change it describes; the CHANGELOG records each release.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README opens with a one-command install and a working client configuration. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp#readme
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/ROADMAP.md — what is planned, what is not, and why.
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md covers the security model, threat mitigations, the assurance case and the remediation thresholds.
external_dependencies_justification: Three runtime dependencies, all declared in package.json and pinned through the committed lockfile.
hardening_justification: The HTTP transport sets X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, a strict Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy and no-store caching on every response including refusals, and HSTS over TLS. Verified by tests against a real listener.
implement_secure_design_justification: A five-layer pipeline — argument validation, path guard, audit, tool, result sanitisation — with the read-only guarantee enforced structurally. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
input_validation_justification: Every tool argument passes a validator before reaching a handler, and app_path additionally passes a symlink-aware containment check that fails closed.
installation_common_justification: `npx -y @shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp`, or install from npm. The README gives one-click configuration for the common MCP clients.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is through npm, which owns the install location. There is no make install honouring DESTDIR or prefix.
interfaces_current_justification: The MCP interface is documented in the README and published by the server itself in its initialize response; a tool-registry integrity test asserts the advertised list and the handler map agree.
internationalization_justification: The server returns structured analysis of source code to a model, not user-facing prose. There are no translatable end-user strings.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Four releases in August 2026, each through the same CI gate.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Every defect fixed since 1.0.1 shipped with a test that fails without the fix — the tool-registry integrity suite, the HTTP 413 delivery, the prototype-pollution guard and the ReDoS patterns are each covered. See the CHANGELOG.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are published from CI with an SLSA provenance attestation signed through Sigstore and recorded by npm, verifiable with `npm audit signatures @shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp`, plus a GitHub build-provenance attestation over the tarball. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
sites_password_security_justification: The project operates no site that accepts passwords. The repository and package pages are GitHub and npm.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests with every change, and the coverage floor for src/utils/ is enforced by CI rather than by convention. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Overall statement coverage is 2.8%. The security-critical layers are covered — src/utils/ at 100% of statements, lines and functions, and the network-facing HTTP transport at 99.5% of lines — but the 820 tool modules under src/tools/ have no tests, and they dominate the count. This is stated openly in the assurance case as the weakest part of the argument, and closing it is the first item on ROADMAP.md.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Dependencies are consumed as ordinary npm packages, not vendored or forked, so each can be updated independently.
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags are annotated but not GPG-signed. The released artefacts themselves carry Sigstore-backed SLSA provenance, which is the signature a consumer can actually verify against the build.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters in the advisory and the CHANGELOG unless they ask otherwise. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md states the private channel, an acknowledgement within 7 days, an assessment within 14, and a fix released before public disclosure. https://github.com/shakaran/symfony-agent-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
